Following the Lumentum / Marvell deal: 

My opinion is that independent Western laser players, like $AAOI, $COHR, and $SIVE became a lot more strategically valuable. 

$MTSI and $SMTC should get some attention too as emerging laser players in 2027. 

If I had to guess: 

1. Companies competing against Marvell, or not in the $NVDA ecosystem bandwagon, such as $AMD, are likely going to rethink their relationship with $LITE.

If getting bottlenecked by Nvidia capacity agreements wasn't enough... Incentives around qualifying + bringing up other laser players, seems very necessary now. 

Since you generally don't want competitors like Marvell to have influence or visibility over your roadmaps, IP, capacity, pricing, etc. even if there is a "firewall".  

2. $MRVL acquiring Lumentum opened pandoras box in a way of acquiring a critical chokepoint all your competitors + buyers use. 

$LITE was used by your major hyperscalers and across AI supply chains. 

Now, your leaders might wonder if weaponizing capacity agreements might not be as effective.... If someone else can just buy the entire company. 

There's only a few major public merchant Western players out there, and I'm also sure many others will want to follow the Marvell / Broadcom route via vertical integration, given I think $MRVL saves around $1B+ in costs/year. 

So M&A premiums likely went up. 

$SMTC was actively looking to buy laser capacity via M&A so I'm sure they're looking at $SIVE given their 100M CW DFB laser expansion + tiny MC. 

$JBL also probably wants to vertically integrate down the road too so $SIVE is also an acquisition target for their 1.6T program. 

$AMD was looking for ELSFP + CW capacity given Nvidia bottlenecks, so I'm sure they've looked at $AAOI. 

can go on and on about other ASIC players (like in Taiwan) that likely are looking at vertical integration too.

Since multiple players use a small subset of laser suppliers, if competitors just go ahead and buys them... 

There's a lot pressure to M&A for their own supply chain defensibility. 

TLDR: Independent laser suppliers should capture a material strategic revaluation since $MRVL + $LITE, sets a new precedent + implications. 

We'll see what happens.

Anthropic says in its amended S-1 that its internal estimates and expectations about FUTURE models indicate that it may "imminently" meet the definition if "dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI".

Under the RSP, this means that Anthropic observes or expects 2x the rate of progress in AI capabilities vs. the rate Anthropic would expect and the fastest rate of extended progress observed over at least 3 model generations without significant AI contributions to AI R&D, plus it's plausible that this doubling is due to automation of research and/or engineering such that it's likely that there will be even greater acceleration.

Note that "2x the rate of progress" means that 2 years of progress would be compressed into 1 year.  So, if Anthropic would have improved its models 9x in one year without AI-enabled acceleration, this threshold would be reached when Anthropic expects to be able to improve its models by 81x in one year (9^2).

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://hackertube.org/

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

You let YouTube's algorithm pick what you watch.
Karpathy replaced it in 2 hours with Claude: 43M Hacker News comments in, 6,454 videos out.

That's why your homepage is clickbait and his isn't.

What he actually did:

→ Claude Code desktop, Opus 5.5 on Medium effort. He says he only talked to Claude and had it do everything.
→ His manual work was 3 browser chores: a Google Cloud API key, a VPS, a domain.
→ Then one instruction: "update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize." Claude did it.
→ No login. Thumbnails are a frame from the middle of the video, not the A/B-tested face.
→ He shared the data as one zip: "point your Claude at it and ask for your own version."

YouTube has thousands of engineers on that feed. Karpathy had Medium effort.

The part people will miss is the signal he picked. YouTube ranks what keeps you watching tonight. HN comments show what people still vouch for years later. Same videos, different question.

And the hard part of the prompt is one distinction: recommended vs. mentioned. "Watch this talk" is a vote. "That talk was wrong" is a mention. Get that wrong and your feed fills with drama.

The prompt to build your own:

"You have a dataset of [comments / bookmarks / newsletters].
Goal: find the [videos / books / tools] people recommend to each other.
Step 1: Label 30 random items as RECOMMEND, MENTION or CRITICIZE. Show me the labels and stop.
Step 2: After I approve, run it on everything. Rank by distinct people recommending each item and how many years they kept doing it. Drop single-recommendation items and one-week spikes.
Step 3: Show the top 20 with your reasoning before building anything.
Step 4: Build one local page: grid, filters by topic and length, no login, likes saved in the browser."

Step 1 is what most people skip. 30 labels now saves you from 6,000 wrong ones later.

AI agents are super dope but also sadly the single greatest existential threat to the internet

the dead internet theory is becoming more and more real every day:

> people are using grok bot to summarize their X feed for them now
> google search traffic to publishers fell 40% in the last year
> people are using AI to summarize their emails

the internet has always run on the deal that you create content → people visit your page → you get paid through ads or subscriptions

agents don’t look at ads... so the fewer human eyeballs the content gets = smaller sponsorship deals

and if publishers and creators can’t get paid, they'll stop creating. the journalism never gets done & the information never exists

I think agents with their own wallets could be a good solution...
